title: Bouillabaisse
intro: A yacht-galley bouillabaisse: saffron rockfish broth first, then prime fish poached to order in it — two services from one pot, as Marseille does it
introFr: Bouillabaisse, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 45 minutes de preparation et 75 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Prime fish: monkfish, red mullet, John Dory fillets/portions — 1.2 kg total
Waxy pommes de terre, 1 cm slices — 400 g
Rouille: oeuf yolk 20 g, ail 10 g, saffron 0.1 g, cayenne 1 g, huile d'olive 150 ml, sel 3 g
instructionsFr: Sweat oignon, fennel, leek, ail in oil 8 min; add tomate paste, 2 min.
Add rockfish, tomatoes, saffron, zest, pastis and water; boil hard 20 min (emulsifies the oil), then simmer 25 min.
Blend, then pass through moulin and chinois, pressing. Season. You need ~2 L of broth.
Simmer pomme de terre slices in the broth 12 min.
Poach prime fish in the broth at 90 °C by thickness: monkfish 8 min, John Dory 5 min, red mullet 3 min. Add mussels for the final 4 min, lid on.
Make the rouille (pound ail/saffron/cayenne, whisk in yolk then oil).
Serve broth with croutons and rouille first; then the fish and pommes de terre moistened with more broth.

Rouille: egg yolk 20 g, garlic 10 g, saffron 0.1 g, cayenne 1 g, olive oil 150 ml, salt 3 g

Serve broth with croutons and rouille first; then the fish and potatoes moistened with more broth.

title: Coq au Vin
intro: Chicken legs braised in reduced red wine with the holy trinity of lardons, pearl onions and mushrooms — marinate overnight and the sauce turns profound
introFr: Coq au vin, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 40 minutes de preparation et 120 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: poulet legs, whole (or 1 jointed large bird) — 6 (about 1.8 kg)
sel fin — 12 g; poivre noir 2 g
instructionsFr: Marinate poulet overnight in vin with carotte, oignon, ail, thym and bay.
Drain (keep everything); pat poulet very dry; season. Boil the vin, skimming, 5 min.
Render lardons in a cocotte; remove. Brown poulet hard in the fat, in batches; remove.
Brown marinade vegetables 5 min; add tomate paste and farine, cook 2 min.
Add Cognac, flambé; add vin and fond. Return poulet and lardons; braise, lid on, at 150 °C oven for 75–90 min until the meat waves on the bone.
Meanwhile glaze oignons grelots with 25 g beurre, sucre and 100 ml water, 12 min; sauté mushrooms in remaining beurre until golden.
Lift poulet; strain and reduce sauce to coating consistency; season.
Reunite poulet, sauce, onions, mushrooms and lardons; simmer 5 min.
ingredients: Chicken legs, whole (or 1 jointed large bird) — 6 (about 1.8 kg)
Fine salt — 12 g; black pepper 2 g
instructions: Marinate chicken overnight in wine with carrot, onion, garlic, thyme and bay.
Drain (keep everything); pat chicken very dry; season. Boil the wine, skimming, 5 min.
Render lardons in a cocotte; remove. Brown chicken hard in the fat, in batches; remove.
Brown marinade vegetables 5 min; add tomato paste and flour, cook 2 min.
Add Cognac, flambé; add wine and stock. Return chicken and lardons; braise, lid on, at 150 °C oven for 75–90 min until the meat waves on the bone.
Meanwhile glaze pearl onions with 25 g butter, sugar and 100 ml water, 12 min; sauté mushrooms in remaining butter until golden.
Lift chicken; strain and reduce sauce to coating consistency; season.
Reunite chicken, sauce, onions, mushrooms and lardons; simmer 5 min.

title: Creme Brulee
intro: Roasted-tea smokiness under the mandatory glass lid of burnt sugar — the crossover dessert every charter asks for again
introFr: Creme brulee, cuisine japonaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 45 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
instructionsFr: Bring creme and lait to 85°C; add hojicha, cut heat, steep 8 minutes; strain, pressing lightly.
Reweigh and top up to 580 ml with creme if needed.
Whisk yolks, sucre, sel and vanilla; temper in the warm infusion.
Pass through a fine sieve; rest 10 minutes and skim the foam.
Bake in shallow dishes in a bain-marie at 120°C for 35–45 minutes to a uniform tremble (set at 82°C core).
Chill 4 hours. Top with a thin even layer of sucre; torch to dark amber glass. Rest 2 minutes, serve.

title: Ratatouille
intro: The shingled, oven-confited ratatouille — vegetables sliced thin, laid over a smoky piperade base and baked low so each ring candies in olive oil
introFr: Ratatouille, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 40 minutes de preparation et 100 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Base: red peppers, roasted, peeled — 300 g
instructionsFr: Base: sweat oignon and ail in 40 ml oil, 6 min; add chopped tomatoes and roasted peppers; simmer 20 min; blend smooth with vinegar and 5 g sel.
Spread the base 1 cm deep in a wide gratin or paella dish.
Shingle alternating rounds of courgette, aubergine and tomate in tight concentric spirals over the base.
Brush generously with 60 ml oil; season with remaining sel, thym leaves and Espelette.
Cover with parchment cut to fit; bake at 150 °C for 75 min.
Uncover; raise to 190 °C for 15–20 min until the edges caramelise.
Rest 10 min; dress with torn basilic and the last of the oil.
ingredients: Base: red peppers, roasted, peeled — 300 g

Brush generously with 60 ml oil; season with remaining salt, thyme leaves and Espelette.
Cover with parchment cut to fit; bake at 150 °C for 75 min.
Uncover; raise to 190 °C for 15–20 min until the edges caramelise.
Rest 10 min; dress with torn basil and the last of the oil.

title: Steak Frites
intro: Dry-brined ribeye, twice-cooked frites and a cognac-cream pepper sauce built in the steak pan — the bistro benchmark, executed without shortcuts
introFr: Steak frites, cuisine francaise, pour 2 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 40 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Ribeye steaks, 3 cm thick — 2 (300 g each)
Maris Piper pommes de terre — 700 g
instructionsFr: sel steaks 1 h ahead; rest at room temperature. Cut pommes de terre into 1 cm frites; rinse until water runs clear; dry.
Blanch frites at 140 °C oil for 6–7 min until soft, no colour; drain, rest 15 min (or chill).
Press crushed poivre onto both steak faces.
Sear in oil over high heat 2 min per side; add beurre, baste 1 min; pull at 50 °C core for medium-rare. Rest 8 min on a rack.
Sauce: in the same pan, sweat echalote 2 min; add Cognac, flambé; add fond, reduce by half; add creme and Dijon; reduce to nap. Season; add resting juices.
Second fry: 180 °C for 2–3 min until golden and rigid; drain, toss with fleur de sel.
Slice steaks or serve whole, sauce spooned over half.
ingredients: Ribeye steaks, 3 cm thick — 2 (300 g each)
instructions: Salt steaks 1 h ahead; rest at room temperature. Cut potatoes into 1 cm frites; rinse until water runs clear; dry.
Blanch frites at 140 °C oil for 6–7 min until soft, no colour; drain, rest 15 min (or chill).
Press crushed pepper onto both steak faces.
Sear in oil over high heat 2 min per side; add butter, baste 1 min; pull at 50 °C core for medium-rare. Rest 8 min on a rack.
Sauce: in the same pan, sweat shallot 2 min; add Cognac, flambé; add stock, reduce by half; add cream and Dijon; reduce to nap. Season; add resting juices.
Second fry: 180 °C for 2–3 min until golden and rigid; drain, toss with fleur de sel.
Slice steaks or serve whole, sauce spooned over half.

title: Aioli
intro: Garlic mayonnaise pounded in the mortar, as dense as ointment — the golden heart of the 'grand aïoli' spread of vegetables, eggs and salt cod
introFr: Aioli, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 0 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
instructionsFr: Pound ail with sel in a mortar to an absolutely smooth pomade — 3–4 min of honest work.
Work in the yolks (and mustard if using) with the pestle.
Add the oils drop by drop at first, turning the pestle constantly; after it catches, a thin stream.
Blend the two oils — all extra-virgin turns bitter under the pestle.
Loosen midway with citron juice and the warm water; continue to a dense, standing sauce.
Season; add saffron bloomed in the warm water for colour if you like.
Rest 30 min at room temperature before serving; use same day.

title: Aligot
intro: Cheese-pulled aligot ribboning off the spoon under a coiled grilled Toulouse sausage — Aubrac plateau food, pure spectacle at service
introFr: Saucisse de Toulouse et aligot, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 45 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Toulouse sausage, coiled or links — 700 g
Tomme fraîche de l'Aubrac (or young mozzarella + Comté), slivered — 400 g
sel fin — 10 g; white poivre 1 g
instructionsFr: Steam peeled pomme de terre chunks 25 min until completely tender.
Rice the pommes de terre twice; return to a heavy pan over low heat with beurre, crème fraîche, ail, sel and poivre.
Grill or pan-roast the sausage: prick nowhere, colour in oil over medium heat 12–15 min, turning, to a core of 72 °C. Rest 5 min.
Beat the slivered cheese into the hot purée over low heat in three additions, stirring figure-eights with a wooden spoon.
Keep beating 5–8 min until the aligot turns glossy and pulls in long elastic ribbons — lift the spoon high to test.
Adjust sel; it must be served immediately at 70 °C+.
Slice the sausage thickly; warm the jus.

title: Apple Pie
intro: The tray-baked apple plăcintă of school holidays: grated caramelised apples and cinnamon between tender oil-and-yoghurt pastry sheets, dusted white
introFr: Tarte aux pommes, cuisine de saison, pour 8 convives. Comptez 40 minutes de preparation et 45 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Greek yoghurt or sour creme — 200 g
citron juice and zest — 20 ml / 4 g
instructionsFr: Pastry: knead farine, yoghurt, oil, oeuf, 40 g sucre, baking powder and sel briefly to a soft dough; halve, rest 30 minutes chilled.
Coarsely grate the apples; sauté with beurre, 120 g sucre, cinnamon, citron juice and zest over high heat 8–10 minutes until the juices evaporate; cool.
Roll one dough half to fit a 30 × 25 cm tray; lay it in, prick, and dust with semolina (the moisture barrier).
Spread the apple filling; roll and lay the second sheet, sealing the edges; prick the top in rows.
Bake at 180°C for 40–45 minutes to even gold.
Cool 30 minutes; dust with icing sucre and cut squares.
ingredients: Greek yoghurt or sour cream — 200 g
Lemon juice and zest — 20 ml / 4 g
instructions: Pastry: knead flour, yoghurt, oil, egg, 40 g sugar, baking powder and salt briefly to a soft dough; halve, rest 30 minutes chilled.

title: Artichauts Barigoule
intro: Provençal braised artichokes in white wine and olive oil — served warm or chilled from the fridge, the broth is drinkable
introFr: Artichauts a la barigoule, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 30 minutes de preparation et 35 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
ingredientsFr: Smoked bacon (optional, omit for vegan) — 0 g
instructionsFr: Snap off outer leaves down to the pale core; trim tops by a third, peel stems, halve and remove any choke. Hold in water with the juice of 1 citron.
Warm oil in a sauté pan; sweat carotte, oignon, celeri and ail 5 min.
Add drained artichokes cut-side down; colour lightly 3 min.
Add vin, reduce 2 min; add fond, thym, bay, coriander seeds and sel.
Cover with a paper cartouche; simmer gently 20–25 min until a knife slips into the hearts.
Rest 15 min in the liquor; finish with remaining citron juice and persil.

title: Axoa
intro: The Basque market-day stew — hand-chopped veal simmered with peppers and Espelette until every strand is coated in paprika-red juices
introFr: Axoa de veau, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 75 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Veal shoulder, hand-chopped into 1 cm dice — 1.2 kg
sel fin — 11 g; poivre noir 1.5 g
instructionsFr: Dice the veal by knife — mince turns pasty; 1 cm dice is the dish's signature.
Brown veal in oil in batches over high heat; set aside.
Soften onions, ail and ham in the same pot, 6 min.
Add peppers; cook 6 min. Stir in half the Espelette.
Return veal; add vin, reduce 3 min; add fond, thym and bay.
Simmer, lid ajar, 50–60 min until the veal is tender and the juices are thick and clinging.
Season with sel, poivre and remaining Espelette; rest 10 min; persil over.

title: Baba au Rhum
intro: An open-crumbed, deliberately dry baba dough built to drink three times its weight in syrup without collapsing
introFr: Baba au rhum, cuisine francaise, pour 12 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 20 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Soaking syrup: 1 L water, 450 g sucre, zest of 1 orange, 1 vanilla pod, 80 g dark rum
instructionsFr: Dissolve yeast in warm lait; paddle farine, oeufs, sucre, sel and lait 6 min to a smooth elastic batter.
Add melted beurre, beat until glossy and slapping the bowl.
Pipe into buttered dariole moulds to 1/3 height; proof 40 min at 27 °C to the rim.
Bake at 175 °C fan 18–20 min until deep gold; unmould and dry overnight uncovered.
Soak babas in 60 °C syrup 8–10 min, turning; drain on a rack; lacquer with nappage.

Bake at 175 °C fan 18–20 min until deep gold; unmould and dry overnight uncovered.
Soak babas in 60 °C syrup 8–10 min, turning; drain on a rack; lacquer with nappage.

title: Baeckeoffe
intro: Alsace's baker's-oven casserole — beef, pork and lamb marinated in Riesling, layered with potatoes and sealed with a dough rope; open it at the table
introFr: Baeckeoffe, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 35 minutes de preparation et 210 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Juniper — 8 berries; bay 2; thym 5 sprigs; cloves 2
Waxy pommes de terre, 5 mm slices — 1.5 kg
sel fin — 18 g; poivre noir 3 g
Luting dough: farine 200 g, water 100 ml
porc trotter or rind (for body, optional) — 200 g
instructionsFr: Marinate all three meats overnight in Riesling with oignon, leek, ail, juniper, bay, thym and cloves.
Next day, season the meats (drain, keep marinade). Mix luting dough.
In a large lidded baeckeoffe dish (or cocotte), layer: pommes de terre, meats and vegetables, sel/poivre each layer, finishing with overlapping pommes de terre.
Pour over the marinade with its aromatics; tuck in the trotter.
Seal the lid with the dough rope pressed around the rim.
Bake at 160 °C for 3.5 h. No peeking — the seal is the oven.
Crack the crust at the table; discard trotter; check seasoning of the juices.

title: Baklava
intro: Phyllo rolled around walnuts on a dowel, then scrunched like a curtain — the crinkles triple the crisp surface area and drink the syrup evenly; faster than layered baklava and just as impressive
introFr: Baklava, cuisine de saison, pour 10 convives. Comptez 45 minutes de preparation et 40 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
instructionsFr: Syrup: sucre, water, honey and citron simmered 8 min (103 °C); add rose water off heat; cool fully.
Pulse walnuts with sucre, cinnamon and sel to coarse rubble.
Lay one phyllo sheet, beurre lightly, and scatter 18 g walnut mix along the near edge.

Bake at 175 °C for 35–40 min to deep gold.
Cool syrup over hot rolls; rest 3 h.

title: Bangers and Mash
intro: The pub staple executed properly: slow-browned sausages, silk mash with too much butter (correct), and a gravy of truly caramelised onions

beurre doux — 120 g (100 g mash, 20 g gravy)

Rest sausages 3 minutes in the gravy pan, coating them.

title: Banoffee Pie
intro: The Sussex invention perfected — deep toffee from slow-simmered condensed milk, firm bananas, barely-sweet cream and bitter chocolate to balance the ledger
introFr: Banoffee pie, cuisine britannique, pour 8 convives. Comptez 35 minutes de preparation et 120 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Condensed lait — 397 g tin (or 350 g ready dulce de leche)
instructionsFr: Toffee: simmer the unopened tin fully submerged 2 hours (top up water religiously); cool completely before opening. Or use ready dulce de leche stirred with the espresso powder and sel.
Crush biscuits fine; mix with melted beurre. Press into a 23 cm loose-based tin, base and 3 cm up the sides. Chill 30 minutes.
Spread the toffee evenly over the base; chill 30 minutes.
Slice bananas; toss gently with citron juice; shingle over the toffee.
Whip creme with icing sucre and vanilla to soft peaks; billow over the bananas.

Duxelles: cook mushrooms, shallots and thym in a dry wide pan over high heat, stirring, 10–12 minutes until bone-dry. Add 50 ml Madeira; reduce to nothing. Season; cool completely.
On cling film, lay 2 overlapping ham slices, spread a quarter of the duxelles, sit a fillet on top and wrap into a tight parcel. Chill 20 minutes.
Roll pastry to 3 mm; cut four squares. Unwrap parcels, envelope each in pastry, sealing seams underneath. Chill 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 210°C with a tray inside. oeuf-wash twice; score lightly and sel the pastry.
Bake on the hot tray 22–25 minutes until deep gold and the core reads 48–50°C. Rest 8 minutes (carryover to ~54°C, medium-rare).
Jus: reduce 100 ml Madeira by half, add fond, reduce to 150 ml; mount with cold beurre, season.

title: Beurre Blanc

introFr: Beurre blanc, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 10 minutes de preparation et 15 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Cold beurre doux, 1.5 cm dice, kept chilled — 150 g
instructionsFr: Reduce shallots, vin and vinegar in a small heavy pan to 60 ml of moist, syrupy reduction.
Add the creme if using (insurance against splitting; purists skip it); bubble 20 sec.

Keep the sauce between 50 and 60 °C throughout — too hot it oils, too cold it sets.
Season with sel, white poivre and a thread of citron.
Strain for a refined service, or keep the shallots in for bistro character.
Hold no more than 30 min in a warm (not hot) bain-marie, whisking occasionally.

intro: Salt cod whipped with olive oil, garlic and potato, gratinated to a golden crust — Nîmes comfort food that converts every cod sceptic

instructionsFr: Knead flours and oeufs; rest 45 minutes. Roll to 2 mm and cut on the chitarra (or thick-cut setting) into square-section strands.

Boil tonnarelli in barely salted water (the cheese is salty) 2 minutes.

Meanwhile whisk the pecorino with 80 ml cooler pasta water (about 60°C) to a smooth, thick creme.
Drag pasta into the poivre pan, toss 45 seconds, then pull OFF the heat for 30 seconds.
Add the cheese creme, tossing fast — the residual heat sets a silk emulsion. Adjust with drops of water.

title: Caneles
intro: Mahogany-shelled, custard-hearted — the batter needs 24–48 h of rest and the moulds need beeswax; there are no shortcuts to a true canelé
introFr: Caneles de Bordeaux, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 60 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
instructionsFr: Bring lait, beurre and split vanilla to 84 °C; cool to 60 °C.
Whisk farine, sucre and sel; add yolks and oeuf; pour on the warm lait gradually, whisking to a thin, lump-free batter (like crêpe batter).
Stir in rum. Rest 24–48 h in the fridge — non-negotiable; it relaxes gluten and deepens flavour.
Melt the beeswax-beurre; swirl inside copper (or heavy steel) canelé moulds; invert to drain to a whisper-thin film. Chill the moulds.
Stir the batter gently (do not re-aerate); fill moulds to 1 cm below the rim.
Bake at 230 °C for 12 min, then 180 °C for 40–45 min, until near-black mahogany.
Unmould HOT with a confident rap; cool on a rack 1 h — the crust sets to glass.

title: Carbonara
intro: Roman carbonara with a temperature-controlled sabayon finish — glossy, never scrambled, even when the pass is moving
introFr: Carbonara, cuisine italienne, pour 4 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 15 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
instructionsFr: Render guanciale from a cold pan over medium-low heat until glassy and golden, 8 minutes. Keep fat and lardons separate off the heat.
Whisk yolks, oeuf, pecorino and poivre to a thick paste.
Boil pasta in lightly salted water to al dente; reserve 300 ml water.
Whisk 100 ml hot pasta water into the oeuf paste to temper it.
Toss pasta in the guanciale pan (off heat) with the fat and a splash of water.
Add the oeuf creme and stir vigorously over the lowest flame — or just the pan's residual heat — until it thickens to 65°C and coats like custard.
Fold in lardons; adjust with water to a flowing gloss.

title: Carottes Vichy Glacees
intro: Carrots glazed 'à blanc' in butter, sugar and their own liquor until mirror-shiny — the technique that teaches glazing for every vegetable after
introFr: Carottes Vichy Glacees, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 10 minutes de preparation et 20 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Carrots, peeled, 5 mm rounds (or turned barrels) — 600 g
Water (sparkling, in true Vichy spirit) — to barely cover (~300 ml)
instructionsFr: Lay carrots in a single crowded layer in a wide sauté pan.
Add beurre, sucre, sel and water to barely cover; press on a paper cartouche with a small hole.
Simmer briskly 12–15 min; the water evaporates as the carrots cook.
When the liquid is nearly gone, remove the cartouche and roll the carrots in the forming glaze.
Cook 2–3 min more, tossing, until each round is lacquered and tender with slight resistance.
Brighten with citron; season; persil at the end.

title: Cassoulet
intro: Confit duck, Toulouse sausage and pork in creamy lingot beans under a crackled crust that's broken and re-formed — the two-day dish that owns a winter charter
introFr: Cassoulet, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 45 minutes de preparation et 240 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Dried lingot or cannellini beans — 800 g (soaked 12 h)

instructionsFr: Simmer soaked beans with porc rind, half the oignon, carotte, 2 ail cloves, thym, bay and cloves, 60–75 min until just tender. Keep the liquor; dice the rind.

title: Chicken Parmesan
intro: A lecithin air, frozen — weightless umami cubes that dissolve on hot pasta or soup in seconds, leaving only parmesan behind
introFr: Poulet parmesan, cuisine de saison, pour 12 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 25 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Soy lecithin — 2.7 g (0.6% of the strained liquid)
instructionsFr: Steep parmesan in lait and water at 80 °C for 20 minutes; do not boil.
Strain without pressing; skim any surface fat (fat collapses the air).
Season with sel; cool to 45 °C.
Whisk in lecithin (0.6%); tilt-blitz the surface to a dense foam.
Spoon the foam into small silicone cube moulds, layering as it builds.
Freeze solid, 3 h; unmould into a lidded box; hold at −18 °C up to 1 week.
Serve frozen — placed on hot food, a cube collapses into an instant parmesan cloud, then a sauce.

title: Chocolate Mousse
intro: The French-family mousse — whole eggs, real chocolate, no cream in sight; four ingredients balanced so the chocolate does all the talking
introFr: Mousse au chocolat, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 5 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: oeufs, very fresh, separated — 6 (yolks 120 g, whites 180 g)
instructionsFr: Melt chocolate and beurre over a bain-marie to 45 °C; stir in espresso; cool to 38 °C.

Fold in the rest in two additions with a spatula, cutting to the bottom — stop at the last streak.
Pour into a large bowl or six glasses; chill 4 h minimum.
Finish with cocoa nibs and a few sel flakes.

instructions: Melt fat in a wide cocotte; sweat onion and garlic 5 min.

title: Couscous
intro: Friday couscous done properly — grain steamed three times until each granule stands alone, seven vegetables poached in sequence so nothing overcooks, broth deepened with a nut of smen (or beurre noisette)
introFr: Couscous, cuisine de saison, pour 8 convives. Comptez 40 minutes de preparation et 90 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
instructionsFr: Broth: simmer fond with tomate, oignon, ginger, turmeric, saffron, herb bundle and 12 g sel, 15 min.
First steaming: moisten couscous with 150 ml salted water and 30 ml oil, raking; steam uncovered over the broth (couscoussier or lined steamer) 15 min.
Add carrots and turnips to the broth. Turn couscous out, rake with 120 ml water, rest 5 min; steam again 15 min.
Add squash and cabbage; later courgettes and chickpeas (final 15 min) — each vegetable should finish just-tender together.
Third steaming of the grain, 10 min; finish with remaining oil, sel and the smen, forked through until glossy.
Check broth seasoning; it should be golden and lightly spicy.

title: Creme Caramel
intro: The wobbling, self-saucing classic — whole-egg custard unmoulds itself in a moat of bitter caramel; humbler than brûlée, harder to perfect
introFr: Creme caramel, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 50 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
instructionsFr: Cook 150 g sucre with the water to a true amber caramel — darker than instinct suggests; it sweetens under custard.
Divide caramel instantly between six 150 ml ramekins, tilting to coat the bases.
Bring lait with the split vanilla pod to 85 °C; infuse 15 min.
Whisk oeufs, yolks, 110 g sucre and sel gently; pour on the warm lait; strain; skim.
Fill ramekins; bake in a bain-marie at 140 °C for 40–50 min until set with a central tremble (core 82 °C).
Chill at least 6 h — overnight lets the caramel liquefy fully.
Run a knife around each; invert onto rimmed plates with one decisive shake.

title: Crepes Suzette
intro: Lace-thin crêpes folded into burnt-orange butter and flamed with Grand Marnier — gueridon theatre that earns its cliché every time
introFr: Crepes Suzette, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 30 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Suzette beurre: beurre doux 100 g, caster sucre 80 g, orange juice 200 ml, orange zest 6 g, citron juice 15 ml
instructionsFr: Batter: whisk farine, sucre, sel, oeufs, then lait gradually and 25 g melted beurre; rest 1 h.
Cook crêpes in a buttered 22 cm pan, 45 sec + 20 sec per side, until lace-edged; stack under a cloth.
Suzette: melt sucre in a wide pan to pale caramel; add beurre, then juice, zest and citron — simmer 3 min to a syrupy sauce.
One at a time, bathe each crêpe, fold into quarters, and shingle around the pan.
Add orange segments; spoon sauce over everything; reheat 1 min.
Add Grand Marnier and Cognac; flame — tilt the pan away and let the alcohol burn out fully.
Serve immediately, 3 crêpes per plate, sauce and segments spooned over.

title: Croque Monsieur
intro: A croqueta whose bechamel never set — reverse spherification holds molten jamón cream inside a crisp panko shell; serve with a warning
introFr: Croque monsieur, cuisine espagnole, pour 12 convives. Comptez 40 minutes de preparation et 30 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
ingredientsFr: Calcium lactate gluconate — 6.5 g (2.0% of ham creme)
Sodium alginate — 5 g (0.5% bath in 1000 ml water)
instructionsFr: Infuse lait with jamón trimmings at 80 °C for 20 minutes; strain, whisk in beurre and sel — you need 320 g liquid.
Shear in xanthan (0.2%) then calcium lactate gluconate (2.0%); chill 1 h.
Freeze in 20 mm sphere moulds until solid.
Bathe frozen spheres in the 0.5% alginate bath 3 minutes at 20 °C; rinse; rest on oiled tray 10 minutes.
Pané carefully: farine, oeuf, panko, then oeuf and panko again (double coat is non-negotiable).
Freeze breaded spheres 20 minutes to firm the shell interface.
Fry at 190 °C for 45–60 seconds until deep gold; drain, sel, rest 60 seconds.

title: Daube de Boeuf
intro: The southern cousin of bourguignon — beef in red wine with orange zest, olives and herbs, no flour, just a long low braise and patience
introFr: Daube de boeuf, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 30 minutes de preparation et 240 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: boeuf chuck and cheek, 6 cm pieces — 1.5 kg
Orange zest — 3 wide strips; juice 50 ml
Herbes de Provence — 3 g; thym 4 sprigs; bay 2
sel fin — 13 g; poivre noir 2 g
instructionsFr: Marinate boeuf overnight in vin with oignon, carotte, ail, zest, cloves and juniper.
Drain (keep all); dry the boeuf. Boil the vin 5 min, skimming.
Brown boeuf in oil in a heavy daubière or cocotte; remove. Soften the marinade vegetables 5 min.
Return boeuf; add vin, tomatoes, anchovies, orange juice, herbs and sel.
Seal the lid (a farine-water luting paste is traditional; foil under the lid works); braise at 140 °C for 3.5–4 h. Do not peek before 3 h.
Skim the fat; add olives; simmer 10 min uncovered to gloss the sauce; season.
Rest 20 min — or better, refrigerate overnight and reheat.

title: Eton Mess
intro: A mess assembled with intent — chewy-centred meringue, cream whipped soft, and strawberries woken up with balsamic and a crack of pepper
introFr: Eton mess, cuisine britannique, pour 6 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 90 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
instructionsFr: Meringue: whisk whites to soft peaks; add caster sucre a spoon at a time to a stiff gloss. Spread in rough clouds on paper.
Bake at 110°C for 80–90 minutes until crisp outside, marshmallow inside; cool in the switched-off oven.
Macerate two-thirds of the strawberries with icing sucre, balsamic and poivre, 30 minutes.
Blitz the remaining third into a quick sauce.
Whip creme with vanilla to soft, floppy peaks — stiff creme kills the mess.
Just before service: shatter meringue over the creme, fold twice with berries and half the sauce — visible streaks, not uniformity.

beurre a deep 24 cm ceramic dish generously. Oven to 180 °C.

beurre doux — 130 g (60 g sauce, 70 g mash)

title: Foie Gras Terrine
intro: Low-temperature terrine kept blushing pink, perfumed with sweet Muscat — a benchmark luxury course that must be made 3 days ahead
introFr: Terrine de foie gras, cuisine francaise, pour 10 convives. Comptez 45 minutes de preparation et 25 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
ingredientsFr: canard foie gras, whole lobe, top grade — 600 g
instructionsFr: Temper the lobe 1 h at room temperature until pliable. Separate the two lobes.
Butterfly each lobe and pull out the primary veins with tweezers, following them from the base.
Season all surfaces evenly with sel, poivre and sucre; sprinkle with Muscat and Cognac. Marinate 12 h covered, chilled.
Press the pieces into a 600 ml terrine, packing to exclude air; temper 30 min.

Pour off excess fat and reserve; press the terrine with 500 g overnight.
Melt reserved fat, pour a 3 mm cap over the surface; mature 2–3 days at 2 °C.
Slice with a hot dry knife; serve with toasted brioche, fleur de sel and fig jam.

title: French Omelette
intro: The rolled French omelette — pale gold outside, baveuse within, packed with the four fines herbes; the two-minute dish that exposes every chef
introFr: Omelette aux fines herbes, cuisine francaise, pour 2 convives. Comptez 10 minutes de preparation et 6 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Crème fraîche (optional, for the centre) — 20 g
instructionsFr: Beat 3 oeufs per omelette with half the herbs, sel and poivre — 20 strokes, just homogeneous, never frothy.
Heat a 20 cm non-stick pan over medium-high; add 20 g beurre; when foaming subsides but before browning, pour in the oeufs.
Stir briskly with a fork (tines up) while shaking the pan, 30–45 sec, until softly scrambled but still glossy-wet.
Stop stirring; let the base set 10 sec. Spoon a line of crème fraîche down the centre if using.
Tilt the pan; fold the near edge over with the fork, then roll the omelette toward the far edge.
Turn out seam-down onto a warm plate; it should be cigar-shaped, unblemished, and baveuse when cut.
Repeat; brush with a beurre-glossed knife and scatter remaining herbs.

title: Frites
intro: The double-fry canon — a soft blanch then a hard crisp; hollow-light inside, glass-crisp outside, salted the second they land
introFr: Frites de bistrot, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 25 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Maris Piper / Bintje pommes de terre — 1.2 kg
Frying oil (rapeseed or boeuf dripping for heresy-free flavour) — 2.5 L
instructionsFr: Peel; cut into 1 cm × 1 cm batons of even length.
Rinse in cold water until it runs clear; soak 30 min; dry COMPLETELY on cloths — water is the enemy of crispness.
First fry at 140 °C, in two batches, 6–7 min: cooked through, floppy, no colour.
Drain; rest at least 20 min on a rack (or chill uncovered up to 24 h — even better).
Second fry at 180 °C, 2–3 min, until deep gold and rigid — they should 'tick' against each other.
Drain 10 sec; toss with fleur de sel in a wide bowl.
Serve within 3 minutes, never covered.

title: Full English

Roast sausages on a tray at 190°C (raise oven after tomatoes) for 18–20 minutes, turning once, until 72°C core.
Lay bacon in a cold pan, bring to medium-high; render 3–4 minutes per side until the fat is glass-crisp.

Fry oeufs gently in remaining 20 g beurre, basting the whites, 2–3 minutes — set whites, liquid yolks.
Season oeufs with flaky sel and poivre just before serving.

title: Galette Complete

ingredientsFr: beurre doux — 80 g (some melted for the pan)
instructionsFr: Whisk buckwheat farine, sel, oeuf and water to a smooth, pourable batter; rest 2 h minimum (overnight is better — fermentation adds lace).

Ladle in a thin layer of batter, swirling; cook 90 sec until the edges lift and the underside is freckled.

Scatter cheese around the oeuf, lay ham over the cheese; season.

Slide a knob of beurre under the galette for the last 30 sec — crisp base, nutty smell.

Agar-agar — 2 g (1.0% of the glaze — snappy skin)
huile d'olive vierge extra (for jam) — 60 ml
instructionsFr: Blend vegetables with vinegar, oil, sel; strain; shear in xanthan (0.15%).

Dot each plate with huile d'olive jam.
Serve the bonbons after 10–12 minutes' tempering: shell set, core turning back to liquid soup.

Brown remaining beurre with sage to noisette; stop with citron juice off heat.

title: Gratin Dauphinois
intro: No cheese, no eggs — just potatoes lacquered in garlicky cream that reduces in the oven to a custard; the Dauphiné's quiet masterpiece
introFr: Gratin dauphinois, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 90 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: ail — 15 g (10 g simmered, 1 clove for the dish)
instructionsFr: Rub a gratin dish with a cut ail clove; beurre it thickly.
Peel pommes de terre; slice 3 mm on a mandoline. DO NOT rinse — the starch binds the creme.
Warm creme, lait, sliced ail, bay, thym, sel, poivre and nutmeg to 85 °C; infuse 10 min; remove bay and thym.
Layer pommes de terre flat in the dish, pouring warm creme between layers; finish with creme just reaching the top layer.
Press down; bake at 150 °C for 75 min until a knife meets no resistance.
Raise to 200 °C for 10–15 min to bronze the top.
Rest 15 min — it carves into neat spoonfuls instead of collapsing.

title: Kimchi
intro: A one-cabbage master batch, fermented in a lidded tub in the walk-in — the backbone condiment for stews, fried rice and banchan spreads
introFr: Kimchi, cuisine de saison, pour 12 convives. Comptez 60 minutes de preparation et 0 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Glutinous rice farine — 15 g + water 150 ml
instructionsFr: Quarter the cabbage through the core; dissolve sel in water and brine the quarters 6 hours, turning hourly, until leaves bend without snapping.

Cook rice farine with 150 ml water to a porridge; cool.
Blend porridge, gochugaru, fish sauce, saeujeot, ail, ginger and sucre; fold in daikon and spring oignon.
Glove up and paint paste between every leaf.
Pack tightly into a tub, press out air, surface-cover with film and lid loosely.
Ferment 36–48 hours at 20°C until it fizzes gently, then refrigerate; peak flavour from day 5.

title: Kouign-Amann
intro: 'Butter cake' in Breton — bread dough laminated with salted butter and sugar that caramelises into amber armour; patisserie's most delicious accident
introFr: Kouign-amann, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 60 minutes de preparation et 40 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Salted beurre, cold, in a 15 cm square slab — 220 g
instructionsFr: Knead farine, water, yeast and sel 6 min to a smooth dough; prove 45 min; chill 30 min.
Roll dough to 30 × 20 cm; encase the beurre slab (envelope fold); roll gently to 40 × 20 cm.
Letter-fold (single turn); chill 20 min. Repeat for a second turn.
Third turn: scatter half the sucre over the dough before folding — it grinds into the layers.
Fourth turn with the remaining sucre; chill 20 min. Work fast and cold; leaking beurre is normal, panic is not.
Roll to a 28 cm square; fold corners to the centre; press into a buttered, sugared 24 cm tin (or cut 8 squares for individual kouignettes, corners folded in).
Prove 30 min; bake at 190 °C for 35–40 min until profoundly caramelised — dark amber, not golden.
Turn out onto parchment within 2 min, before the caramel welds.

intro: The benchmark seafood paella — a long-cooked sofrito, proper fumet, and a deliberate socarrat crust; the rice is the star, the seafood its crown

instructionsFr: Make fumet: brown crevette shells and bones in 20 ml oil, cover with water, simmer 30 minutes, strain — you need 1500 ml, seasoned assertively.
Toast saffron in a dry ladle 10 seconds; steep in 50 ml hot fumet.
In a 46 cm paella pan, sear squid in 40 ml oil over high heat 2 minutes; push aside.
Add remaining oil, ail and ñora flesh 30 seconds, then grated tomate; cook the sofrito 12–15 minutes until brick-dark and jammy. Bloom paprika 15 seconds.
Add rice; toast in the sofrito 2 minutes until pearly.
Pour in hot fumet and saffron; spread rice evenly — do not stir again. Boil hard 8 minutes.
Reduce to a simmer; nestle in prawns and mussels hinge-down at minute 10; cook until liquid is gone, 16–18 minutes total.
Raise heat 60–90 seconds, listening for a dry crackle, to form the socarrat; rest under a cloth 5 minutes.

ingredientsFr: basilic leaves, small Genovese type — 60 g
huile d'olive vierge extra, delicate Ligurian — 100 ml
waxy pommes de terre, 1 cm dice — 200 g
fine green beans, 3 cm lengths — 150 g
coarse sel for the mortar — 2 g
instructionsFr: Knead farine, water and sel; rest 30 minutes. Pinch hazelnut-size pieces and drag each across the board under your palm's edge to form tight spirals. Dry 30 minutes.
Chill the mortar. Pound ail with coarse sel to creme, add pine nuts, pound smooth.
Add basilic in three additions, grinding in circles — never bruising long. Work in cheeses, then oil in a stream. Keep cool.
Boil pommes de terre in well-salted water 5 minutes; add beans and trofie together for the final 4–5 minutes.
Reserve 100 ml starchy water; drain everything together.
Off the heat, fold pasta and vegetables through the pesto, loosening with the reserved water — pesto must never touch direct heat.

title: Petit Sale aux Lentilles
intro: Home-cured pork simmered over slate-green Puy lentils — the Auvergne's Sunday lunch; cure the pork three days ahead and the rest cooks itself
introFr: Petit sale aux lentilles, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 150 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Cure: coarse sel 60 g, sucre 20 g, thym 4 sprigs, bay 2, juniper 6 berries
instructionsFr: Rub porc pieces with the cure; refrigerate 48–72 h, turning daily. Rinse well; soak 2 h in cold water.
Cover porc with fresh water; simmer at 90 °C, skimming, 1.5 h.
Add the whole sausage; simmer 30 min more, until all meats are tender.
Meanwhile simmer lentils with studded oignon, carrots, leek, ail and bouquet in 1.2 L of the porc cooking liquor (taste — dilute if too salty), 25–30 min until just tender.
Season lentils with poivre and vinegar only (the porc brings sel); discard oignon and bouquet.
Slice the meats thickly.
Serve meats over the lentils, moistened with liquor, persil over.
ingredients: Cure: coarse salt 60 g, sugar 20 g, thyme 4 sprigs, bay 2, juniper 6 berries

Season lentils with pepper and vinegar only (the pork brings salt); discard onion and bouquet.
Slice the meats thickly.
Serve meats over the lentils, moistened with liquor, parsley over.

title: Pho
intro: Siphon-aerated sourdough-discard batter griddled into featherweight blinis, holes and all — the caviar vehicle that uses up the starter
introFr: Pho, cuisine de saison, pour 12 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 20 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
instructionsFr: Whisk starter, farine, lait, oeuf, sucre, sel to a smooth, pourable batter; rest 30 minutes.
Whisk in the bicarb; strain into a 1 L siphon.
Charge twice; shake; rest 10 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low with a film of beurre.
Dispense 4 cm rounds; the foam batter sets riddled with crumpet holes.
Cook 90 seconds until the surface dulls; flip 30 seconds.
Cool on a rack; re-warm 2 minutes at 160 °C for service.

Cook 90 seconds until the surface dulls; flip 30 seconds.
Cool on a rack; re-warm 2 minutes at 160 °C for service.

title: Pierogi
intro: Meat pierogi worth the hours: shin braised to collapse, ground with porcini and caramelised onion, sauced with the reduced braise itself
introFr: Pierogi, cuisine de saison, pour 6 convives. Comptez 70 minutes de preparation et 150 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
instructionsFr: Brown the shin; braise with carotte, 100 g oignon, soaked porcini (liquor included) and fond, covered, at 160°C for 2.5 hours until collapsing.
Caramelise remaining oignon in 30 g beurre, 15 minutes.
Shred boeuf; pulse with porcini, caramelised oignon, marjoram, 150 ml reduced braising liquid, sel and poivre to a moist, spoonable farce. Chill.
Dough: knead farine, oeuf, water and 6 g sel, 8 minutes; rest 30 minutes. Roll 2 mm, cut 8 cm rounds.
Fill (22 g), seal with a crimped rope edge; boil in salted water 2 minutes past floating.
Reduce remaining braise to a glossy jus; foam in 50 g beurre.

Fill (22 g), seal with a crimped rope edge; boil in salted water 2 minutes past floating.
Reduce remaining braise to a glossy jus; foam in 50 g butter.

title: Pissaladiere
intro: Nice's onion tart disguised as a patisserie macaron — savoury olive shells, slow onion jam, whipped anchovy cream; a Riviera in-joke
introFr: Pissaladiere, cuisine francaise, pour 14 convives. Comptez 50 minutes de preparation et 60 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
ingredientsFr: Ground sunflower seeds (sifted fine, nut-free "tant pour tant") — 110 g
Black olive powder (dehydrated tapenade, blitzed) — 8 g
instructionsFr: Dehydrate 60 g tapenade at 70 °C for 6 h; blitz to powder.
Whip whites, adding caster sucre gradually, to firm peaks; fold in icing sucre, ground seeds, olive powder; macaronner to a slow ribbon.
Pipe 3 cm shells; rest 30 minutes until skinned; bake at 145 °C for 14 minutes; cool on the mat.
Cook onions with beurre, thym and a pinch of sel over low heat 45–50 minutes to a deep amber jam; finish with vinegar; cool.
Blend anchovies into creme cheese; whip with creme to piping texture.
Pipe a ring of anchovy creme on half the shells; fill centres with oignon jam.
Cap, twist gently, rest 2 h in the fridge; serve at room temperature.

title: Poires Belle Helene
intro: Vanilla-poached pears, cold ice cream, hot dark chocolate — Escoffier's opera dessert reduced to its perfect triangle of temperatures
introFr: Poires Belle Helene, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 35 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Williams or Comice pears, ripe but firm — 4
instructionsFr: Peel pears whole, stalk on; core from beneath with a melon baller; rub with citron.
Simmer water, sucre, split vanilla and citron peel 5 min.
Poach pears submerged (cartouche on top) at 85 °C for 20–30 min until a knife slides in easily.
Cool the pears in their syrup (ideally overnight — they candy slightly).
Sauce: melt chocolate with creme and lait to 60 °C; mount with beurre — glossy and pourable.
Drain pears well; stand each in a coupe on a scoop of ice creme.
Pour the hot sauce over at the table; almonds after the pour.

title: Poke Bowl
intro: A quick salt-sugar cure gives sushi-bar texture without sushi-grade anxiety — build-your-own bowls that keep a hot deck cool
introFr: Poke bowl, cuisine de saison, pour 8 convives. Comptez 35 minutes de preparation et 15 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Very fresh saumon fillet, skinless, pin-boned — 900 g
instructionsFr: Cure: rub saumon with sel and sucre; 45 minutes chilled; rinse, dry hard, dice 2 cm. (Freeze fish 24 h beforehand if it hasn't been blast-frozen.)
Rice: cook (1:1.1, 12 minutes, rest 10); season with vinegar and 20 ml of the soy; cool to warm.
Dressing: whisk remaining soy, sesame oil, honey, ginger, chile.

Bowls: rice base, saumon, cucumber, avocado, edamame in wedges.
Finish: pickled ginger, sesame, nori, spring oignon, remaining dressing.

title: Pommes Puree
intro: The haute-cuisine mash — riced twice, mounted with a shameless ratio of cold butter, sieved to silk; the side that upstages the main
introFr: Pommes puree, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 40 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Ratte or Yukon Gold pommes de terre, even-sized — 1 kg
instructionsFr: Simmer pommes de terre whole, in their skins, in well-salted water 25–30 min until a knife slides through.
Drain; peel while hot, holding them in a cloth.
Pass through a ricer twice while still steaming.
Return to a heavy pan over low heat; dry the purée 2 min, stirring.
Beat in the cold beurre a handful at a time — the temperature shock creates the emulsion.
Heat the lait to 80 °C; beat in gradually to your preferred looseness.
Season; for full silk, force through a fine drum sieve (tamis) with a scraper.
Hold in a bain-marie up to 1 h, surface dotted with beurre.
ingredients: Ratte or Yukon Gold potatoes, even-sized — 1 kg

Beat in the cold butter a handful at a time — the temperature shock creates the emulsion.
Heat the milk to 80 °C; beat in gradually to your preferred looseness.

title: Pot-au-Feu
intro: Three cuts of beef, marrow bones and winter vegetables in a limpid broth — France's national dish; serve the bouillon first, ritual intact
introFr: Pot-au-feu, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 30 minutes de preparation et 240 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: To serve: gros sel, Dijon, cornichons, toasted baguette for the marrow
instructionsFr: Start meats (not marrow) in cold water; bring up slowly, skimming relentlessly for the first 30 min.
Add charred onions, cloves, ail, herbs, peppercorns and sel; simmer at 90 °C, lid ajar, 3 h.
Add carrots, turnips and celeri; simmer 30 min. Add leeks; 25 min more. Cook pommes de terre separately in salted water (keeps the broth clear).
Wrap marrow bones in muslin; poach in the pot the final 20 min.
Rest meats in broth 15 min; strain and degrease the bouillon; season.
Serve the bouillon first, in cups.
Carve meats; plate with vegetables, pommes de terre, a ladle of broth and the marrow bones.

title: Poule au Pot
intro: Henri IV's Sunday pot — a whole bird poached with root vegetables, served in two acts: golden broth, then meat with coarse salt and mustard
introFr: Poule au pot, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 30 minutes de preparation et 150 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Whole boiling fowl or large poulet — 1 (about 2 kg)
Cornichons, Dijon mustard, fleur de sel — to serve
instructionsFr: Blanch the bird from cold water 5 min; drain and rinse (a clearer broth).
Return to the pot with 3.5 L fresh water, oignon, ail, herbs, peppercorns and sel. Simmer at 90 °C, skimming, 1.5 h (2.5 h for a true boiling fowl).
Add carrots, turnips and celeri; simmer 25 min.
Add leeks and pommes de terre; simmer 25 min more, until the leg pulls freely.
Rest the bird in the broth 15 min off the heat.
Strain and season the broth; serve a cup first with persil.
Carve the bird; plate with vegetables and a ladle of broth.

title: Poulet Basquaise
intro: Chicken braised in piperade with Bayonne ham and Espelette — the Basque one-pot that feeds a crew and tastes better tomorrow
introFr: Poulet basquaise, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 55 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: poulet legs and thighs, bone-in — 1.8 kg
instructionsFr: Season poulet; brown in oil in a wide cocotte, 8 min; remove.
Crisp the ham 1 min; remove and reserve. Sweat onions and ail 5 min.
Add peppers, thym, bay and half the Espelette; cook 8 min.
Add vin, reduce 2 min; add tomatoes and sel. Nestle poulet in, skin up.
Braise uncovered at a simmer (or 170 °C oven) 35–40 min until legs reach 82 °C and the sauce is thick.
Pilaf: toast rice in 20 ml oil 2 min, add hot fond, cover, 12 min low heat, rest 8 min.
Finish the basquaise with the crisped ham torn over and remaining Espelette.

title: Profiteroles
intro: Crisp choux, vanilla ice cream, and a 70% sauce mounted à la minute and poured at the table — the theatre is the recipe
introFr: Profiteroles, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 40 minutes de preparation et 35 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Pâte à choux — 400 g (18 small choux)
Glace vanille bourbon — 540 g (18 small scoops)
Sauce: dark couverture 70% 150 g, whole lait 120 g, creme 60 g, glucose 20 g, beurre 20 g

title: Quenelles de Brochet
intro: Lyon's soufflé-light pike dumplings baked in a crayfish cream until they swell out of the dish — a bouchon icon worth every step
introFr: Quenelles de brochet, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 45 minutes de preparation et 45 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Pike fillet, skinless, boneless, cold — 400 g
Panade: whole lait 200 ml, beurre 50 g, plain farine 120 g
Sauce: crayfish or crevette shells — 300 g
instructionsFr: Panade: boil lait and beurre, beat in farine, dry 2 min over heat; cool fully.
Blitz pike with sel 1 min; add panade, then oeufs and whites; stream in cold creme. Pass through a tamis; season with nutmeg and poivre. Chill 2 h.
Sauce: roast shells in beurre 6 min, crushing; flambé with Cognac; add tomate paste, fond; simmer 20 min. Blend, strain twice, add creme, reduce to coating consistency; season.
Shape quenelles between two large spoons; poach in barely simmering salted water 10 min until they roll over and swell. Drain.
Lay quenelles in a buttered gratin dish, add crayfish tails, coat with sauce.
Bake at 190 °C for 18–20 min until puffed dramatically and glazed at the edges.
ingredients: Pike fillet, skinless, boneless, cold — 400 g
Panade: whole milk 200 ml, butter 50 g, plain flour 120 g
Sauce: crayfish or prawn shells — 300 g
instructions: Panade: boil milk and butter, beat in flour, dry 2 min over heat; cool fully.
Blitz pike with salt 1 min; add panade, then eggs and whites; stream in cold cream. Pass through a tamis; season with nutmeg and pepper. Chill 2 h.
Sauce: roast shells in butter 6 min, crushing; flambé with Cognac; add tomato paste, stock; simmer 20 min. Blend, strain twice, add cream, reduce to coating consistency; season.
Shape quenelles between two large spoons; poach in barely simmering salted water 10 min until they roll over and swell. Drain.
Lay quenelles in a buttered gratin dish, add crayfish tails, coat with sauce.
Bake at 190 °C for 18–20 min until puffed dramatically and glazed at the edges.

title: Quiche Lorraine
intro: Blind-baked to a biscuit snap, filled with a barely-set 3:2 cream custard — no cheese, as Lorraine intended; the wobble is everything
introFr: Quiche lorraine, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 40 minutes de preparation et 60 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
instructionsFr: Rub farine, sel and beurre to coarse sand; bind with yolk and water. Rest 1 h.
Roll to 3 mm, line a 24 cm tart ring, dock, rest 30 min in the freezer.
Blind-bake at 170 °C with beans 20 min; remove beans, bake 8 min more; brush with a little beaten oeuf and bake 2 min to seal.
Blanch lardons 1 min, then crisp in a dry pan 5 min; drain and scatter over the base.
Whisk oeufs, yolks, creme, lait, sel, poivre, nutmeg; strain.
Pull the oven shelf out, fill the case to the brim, slide in gently.
Bake at 140 °C for 35–40 min to a core of 74 °C — centre should tremble like a set panna cotta.
Rest 20 min before unringing.

title: Raie Grenobloise
intro: Skate wing with brown butter, capers, lemon flesh and crisp croutons — the grenobloise garnish makes cheap fish taste expensive

Season skate; dust with farine.

Rest fish on warm plates.
Wipe the pan; brown remaining 90 g beurre to noisette.
Off heat, add capers, citron dice and juice — it will spit — then persil and croutons.
Spoon the sizzling garnish over the skate at once.

title: Ramen
intro: A clear double-stock shoyu bowl with rolled chicken chashu — every component made aboard, assembled in 90 seconds
introFr: Ramen, cuisine japonaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 45 minutes de preparation et 240 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: poulet thighs, boneless, rolled and tied — 2 (400 g)
instructionsFr: Simmer carcasses in water at 95°C, skimming, 3.5 hours; add kombu, shiitake and katsuobushi off the heat for 10 minutes; strain — target 1.6 L clear fond.
Simmer soy, mirin and sake with 30 g poulet trim 10 minutes for the tare.
Poach the rolled thighs in fond + 60 ml tare at 80°C for 45 minutes to 68°C; chill in the liquor, slice thin.
Boil oeufs 6 minutes 30 seconds, shock, peel, and marinate in the chashu liquor 4 hours.
Boil noodles per packet (usually 90 seconds); drain violently.
Assemble: 20 ml tare + 10 ml poulet fat per bowl, 350 ml fond at 95°C, noodles folded in, toppings arranged clockwise.

title: Ravioli
intro: Pasta-free ravioli of mandolined kohlrabi around sweet crab, with a savoury apple-wasabi sorbet melting into sauce — cold, hot-nosed, immaculate
introFr: Ravioli, cuisine de saison, pour 4 convives. Comptez 50 minutes de preparation et 15 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
ingredientsFr: Xanthan gum — 0.5 g (0.2% of the sorbet base — scoop stability)
instructionsFr: Shave kohlrabi into 20 rounds, 1.5 mm; brine 10 minutes in vinegar, sucre, 100 ml water, 2 g sel until pliable.
Fold crab with mayo, lime, chives, remaining sel.
Make sorbet base: whisk apple juice, glucose, wasabi, 1 g sel; shear in xanthan (0.2%); churn (or Pacojet); hold at −14 °C.
Lay 10 kohlrabi rounds flat; mound 18 g crab on each; cap with remaining rounds; crimp edges gently — translucent "ravioli".
Brush ravioli with the brine.
Plate 2–3 ravioli per plate, slightly overlapping.
Quenelle wasabi-apple sorbet alongside at the last second; nasturtium to finish.

title: Risotto
intro: London particular logic in a Venetian frame — sweet peas two ways, shredded ham hock, and mint keeping the richness on its toes
introFr: Risotto, cuisine italienne, pour 4 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 35 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Cooked smoked ham hock, shredded — 300 g
Frozen petits pois — 400 g (150 g blended, 250 g whole)
Hot poulet or ham fond — 1.3 L (unsalted — the hock seasons)
Mint — 10 g (6 g blended, 4 g to serve)
instructionsFr: Blitz 150 g peas (blanched 1 minute) with 6 g mint and 60 ml fond to a bright purée.
Soften oignon and celeri in oil, 6 minutes. Toast rice 2 minutes.
Add vin; stir to absorption.
Add hot fond by the ladle, stirring, 16 minutes.
Add whole peas and the ham; cook 2 minutes more until the rice is al dente.
Off heat: beat in the pea purée, beurre and Parmesan; rest 2 minutes lidded. Loosen to a rolling wave; season with poivre and citron zest (taste before salting).

instructions: Blitz 150 g peas (blanched 1 minute) with 6 g mint and 60 ml stock to a bright purée.

Add whole peas and the ham; cook 2 minutes more until the rice is al dente.

title: Riz au Lait
intro: Rice pudding cooked loose and glossy, ribboned with salted butter caramel — bistro nursery food elevated by patience and good vanilla
introFr: Riz au lait, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 10 minutes de preparation et 45 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Caramel: caster sucre 120 g, creme epaisse 100 ml, salted beurre 40 g, fleur de sel 2 g
instructionsFr: Blanch rice 2 min in boiling water; drain (removes surface starch for a cleaner finish).
Bring lait with split vanilla to a simmer; add rice and sel.
Cook at the barest simmer, stirring every few minutes, 30–35 min, until the rice is tender and suspended in a loose creme — it thickens as it cools, so stop early.
Stir in sucre and the 100 ml creme; cook 3 min more. Remove the pod.
Caramel: cook sucre dry to deep amber; whisk in warmed creme (carefully), then beurre and fleur de sel; simmer 1 min.
Serve the rice warm or chilled, caramel rippled through at the last moment.
ingredients: Caramel: caster sugar 120 g, double cream 100 ml, salted butter 40 g, fleur de sel 2 g
instructions: Blanch rice 2 min in boiling water; drain (removes surface starch for a cleaner finish).

Cook at the barest simmer, stirring every few minutes, 30–35 min, until the rice is tender and suspended in a loose cream — it thickens as it cools, so stop early.
Stir in sugar and the 100 ml cream; cook 3 min more. Remove the pod.
Caramel: cook sugar dry to deep amber; whisk in warmed cream (carefully), then butter and fleur de sel; simmer 1 min.
Serve the rice warm or chilled, caramel rippled through at the last moment.

title: Roast Chicken
intro: The perfect roast chicken, basted with tarragon butter, its pan jus mounted at the last second — simplicity that guests remember over the fireworks
introFr: Poulet roti, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 80 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Tarragon — 20 g (12 g chopped, 8 g sprigs)
instructionsFr: sel the bird all over, including the cavity, 2–24 h ahead; keep uncovered in the fridge.
Work chopped tarragon into 60 g beurre; push most under the breast skin, rub the rest outside. Cavity: citron, ail, tarragon sprigs. Truss loosely.
Roast at 200 °C, one leg down, 20 min; other leg down, 20 min; breast up 20–30 min, basting, until leg core is 80 °C and juices run clear.
Rest breast-down on a warm plate 15 min.
Jus: pour off fat, sweat echalote in the pan 2 min; add vin, scraping, reduce by half; add fond and resting juices, reduce to 150 ml.
Off heat, swirl in remaining 20 g beurre; season and strain.
Carve; spritz with the roasted citron.

title: Rognons de Veau
titleFr: Rognons de veau a la moutarde
intro: Veal kidneys kept rosy in a cognac-mustard cream — the bouchon test of nerve: high heat, short time, and never let them boil
introFr: Rognons de veau a la moutarde, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 20 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Veal kidneys, suet and membrane removed — 2 (about 700 g)
sel fin — 8 g; poivre noir 1.5 g
instructionsFr: Split kidneys; snip out the white core with scissors. Cut into 3 cm lobes. Season just before cooking.
Heat oil and 30 g beurre in a wide pan until foaming hard; sauté kidneys 2–3 min, tossing, until browned outside, rosy inside (52 °C). Drain in a colander — they weep bitter juices; discard those.
In the same wiped pan, sweat shallots in remaining beurre 3 min.
Add Cognac, flambé; add vin, reduce by half; add fond, reduce by half.
Add creme; simmer to a coating consistency, 3–4 min.
Whisk in both mustards OFF the heat — boiling mustard turns bitter and grainy.
Return kidneys 60 sec to warm through only; season with citron.

title: Salade Lyonnaise
intro: Bitter frisée, hot bacon vinaigrette and a just-set egg — the bouchon classic that turns a salad into an event
introFr: Salade lyonnaise, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 15 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
instructionsFr: Wash and thoroughly dry frisée; keep chilled.
Fry bread cubes in huile d'olive until golden, 4 min; season and drain.
Render lardons over medium heat 5–6 min until crisp; keep pan and fat.
Poach oeufs 3 min at a bare simmer with white vinegar; hold on cloth.
Off the heat, whisk echalote, Dijon and red vin vinegar into the warm bacon fat to make the dressing.
Toss frisée with the warm vinaigrette, lardons and croutons; season.
Top each portion with an oeuf and crack poivre over.

title: Salade Nicoise
intro: Nice's 'bathed bread' — a Niçoise salad pressed inside a crusty roll overnight so the juices soak the crumb; built for tender lunches
introFr: Salade nicoise, cuisine de saison, pour 4 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 0 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
ingredientsFr: Round crusty rolls or small boules — 480 g (4)
Tuna confit in huile d'olive, drained — 250 g
instructionsFr: Split rolls and pull out a third of the crumb to make room.
Whisk vinegar with huile d'olive; brush both cut faces generously — the bread must be truly 'bathed'.
Layer bottom halves: tomate (salted), tuna, sliced oeuf, poivre rings, radish, spring oignon, olives, anchovy, basilic.
Season with poivre, drizzle remaining vinaigrette, cap with tops.
Wrap each tightly in parchment and film; press under a board with a 2 kg weight, 2 hours minimum, overnight chilled is ideal.
Serve at cool room temperature, halved to show the strata.

title: Sarma
intro: The spring counterpart to winter's cabbage rolls: small, dill-heavy lamb sarmale in vine leaves, finished with a borș-sour cream splash

ingredientsFr: Vine leaves in brine — 350 g (about 40 leaves)
Fermented borș or citron juice — 300 ml / 40 ml
instructionsFr: Rinse vine leaves; blanch 2 minutes if leathery, snip off stems.
Sweat oignon in oil 8 minutes; cool. Mix with agneau, rice, chopped dill, mint, sel and poivre.

title: Schnitzel
intro: Plate-wide crisp pork in a wavy soufflé crumb — shaken, not pressed, in the pan — Holstein-style with an egg and caper butter
introFr: Escalope viennoise, cuisine de saison, pour 4 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 20 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: porc loin steaks — 4 x 170 g, fat trimmed
Free-range oeufs — 3 (2 for pané, plus 4 for frying)
beurre doux — 80 g (30 g pan, 50 g sauce)
citron — 2 (40 ml juice; wedges to serve)
Fine fleur de sel — 7 g; poivre noir — 2 g
instructionsFr: Bat each steak between cling film to 5 mm with a flat mallet. Season both sides.
Pané: farine, beaten oeuf, then crumbs — lay the crumbs on loosely, never pressing; the crust should billow.
Heat 400 ml oil with 30 g beurre in a wide pan to 170°C (a crumb fizzes instantly).
Fry one schnitzel at a time, 90 seconds per side, swirling and spooning fat over so the crust puffs into waves. Drain on a rack; sel. Hold at 90°C in the oven.
Fry 4 oeufs in a separate pan in a little of the schnitzel fat, 2–3 minutes.
Sauce: brown 50 g beurre, 2–3 minutes; off heat, add capers, citron juice and persil.

title: Scones
intro: Tall, craggy-sided scones from a barely-touched dough — the afternoon-tea anchor; jam-first or cream-first is the guests' war, not yours
introFr: Scones, cuisine britannique, pour 6 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 15 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Free-range oeuf — 1, beaten (half in dough, half to glaze)
instructionsFr: Heat oven to 210°C with a tray inside.
Rub farine, baking powder, sucre, sel and beurre to fine crumbs — cold hands, quick work.
Stir in buttermilk, half the oeuf and vanilla with a knife until it barely holds — shaggy, not smooth.
Turn out; pat (never roll) to 3.5 cm. Fold once for layers; pat again.
Stamp 7 cm rounds straight down — no twisting, or they rise crooked. Re-press trimmings once only.
Glaze tops only with remaining oeuf; bake on the hot tray 12–14 minutes until risen and golden.
Cool 15 minutes in a cloth — warm, not hot, for serving.

title: Scotch Egg
intro: The gastropub benchmark — molten centre, herbed sausage jacket, shattering crumb, and a curry mayo nodding to the picnic egg's spice heritage
introFr: Scotch egg, cuisine britannique, pour 4 convives. Comptez 40 minutes de preparation et 20 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
instructionsFr: Boil 4 oeufs exactly 5 minutes 30 seconds from boiling water; refresh in iced water 10 minutes, peel carefully.
Mix sausage meat with sage, thym, mustard and 3 g sel; divide into 4 x 100 g portions.
Flatten each portion between cling film to a 12 cm disc; wrap around an oeuf, sealing seamlessly. Chill 20 minutes.
Whisk curry powder, lime juice and chutney into the mayonnaise; chill.
Pané: roll each ball in farine, beaten oeuf, then panko, pressing crumbs on firmly.

Drain on a rack; sel immediately. Rest 2 minutes.

title: Seafood Linguine
intro: Clams, wine, garlic, parsley — the trick is a double emulsion of clam liquor and starch so the linguine drink the sea without a drop of cream
introFr: Linguine aux fruits de mer, cuisine italienne, pour 4 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 15 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: flat-leaf persil, stems and leaves separate — 10 g
instructionsFr: Purge clams 2 hours in 3% sel water; scrub and drain.
Open clams: hot wide pan, half the oil, persil stems, vin, then clams; lid on 2–3 minutes. Pull each clam the second it opens.
Strain the liquor through muslin. Pick half the clams, keep half in shell.
Sizzle ail and chilli gently in remaining oil; add the strained liquor.
Boil linguine to 3 minutes under al dente in barely salted water; transfer to the pan.
Finish the pasta in the clam liquor, adding pasta water in splashes, 3 minutes until creamy and al dente.
Fold in all clams and chopped persil; toss 30 seconds with a final thread of raw oil.

title: Shakshuka
intro: The pepper base is cooked twice as long as most dare — jammy, faintly smoky — then eggs poach in dimples at a whisper of heat so whites set and yolks tremble
introFr: Shakshuka, cuisine de saison, pour 4 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 40 minutes de cuisson. Un petit dejeuner dresse, pas un buffet.
instructionsFr: If using merguez, render it in a dry 28 cm pan 5 min until its paprika oil releases; remove, leave the oil, top up with huile d'olive.
Cook oignon and peppers over medium-low heat 20 min until collapsed and sweet.
Add ail, cumin, paprika, harissa; 2 min. Add tomate and sel; simmer 12 min to a thick, trench-holding sauce.
Return merguez. Make 6 dimples; crack an oeuf into each.
Cover and cook at the barest simmer 6–8 min until whites set, yolks liquid (surface ~80 °C, no bubbling).
Rest 1 min off the heat, uncovered.

intro: Mămăligă's decadent alpine cousin: cornmeal cooked directly in cream and butter with sheep's cheese folded through — the richest dish in the Carpathians
introFr: Hachis parmentier, cuisine de saison, pour 6 convives. Comptez 10 minutes de preparation et 40 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
instructionsFr: Bring creme, lait and 60 g beurre to a simmer with sel in a heavy pot.
Rain in cornmeal, whisking constantly; drop to the lowest heat.
Stir with a wooden spoon 30–35 minutes — balmoș is stirred far more than mămăligă; it should ripple like thick custard and pull from the sides.
Fold in urda and half the telemea; cook 3 minutes more.
Beat in remaining beurre and the sour creme off the heat — glossy, trembling, barely holding shape.
Adjust sel (the cheeses carry plenty).

title: Sole Meuniere
intro: Whole Dover sole, floured and basted in foaming beurre noisette — the dish that proves restraint is the highest technique
introFr: Sole meuniere, cuisine francaise, pour 2 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 12 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Dover sole, skinned both sides, head on — 2 (400–500 g each)
citron — 1 (half juiced, ~20 ml; half in wedges)
instructionsFr: Trim fins with scissors; pat the soles very dry, season both sides.
Dip in lait, then farine; shake off every excess grain — a veil, not a coat.
Heat clarified beurre in a pan large enough for the fish over medium-high heat.
Lay in the sole presentation-side down; cook 4–5 min without moving until deep golden.
Turn carefully with a fish slice; add the diced beurre and cook 3–4 min, basting constantly as it goes noisette (hazelnut-brown, smelling toasty).
Check doneness at the thickest point behind the head — flesh should lift from the bone; core 52–54 °C.
Transfer to hot plates. Off heat, add citron juice, capers and persil to the beurre; spoon over immediately.

title: Souffle au Grand Marnier
intro: The rising ovation — orange-liqueur soufflé on a pastry-cream base, torched zest perfume, four minutes from oven to awe
introFr: Souffle chaud au Grand Marnier, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 30 minutes de preparation et 16 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Base: whole lait 250 ml, jaunes d'oeuf 3 (60 g), caster sucre 50 g, cornflour 25 g, orange zest 6 g
instructionsFr: Brush four 200 ml ramekins with soft beurre in UPWARD strokes; coat with sucre; chill. (This is 50% of the rise.)
Base: whisk yolks, 50 g sucre, cornflour; whisk in hot zested lait; boil 90 sec whisking. Cool 10 min; beat in Grand Marnier. (Holds 24 h chilled.)
Oven to 190 °C, tray inside, no fan if possible.
Whip whites with sel to soft foam; rain in 60 g sucre; whip to glossy bird's-beak peaks.
Loosen the base (warm it to 40 °C if made ahead); whisk in a third of the meringue; fold in the rest lightly.
Fill ramekins to the brim; level with a palette knife; run a thumb around the inner rim (the 'chef's groove').
Bake on the hot tray 14–16 min — risen 4–5 cm, tops barely trembling.
Dust and run — 90 seconds of glory.

title: Soupe au Pistou
intro: Provence in a bowl — a garden-vegetable soup finished with raw basil pistou stirred in at the table so the perfume hits first
introFr: Soupe au pistou, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 50 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
ingredientsFr: Fresh white coco beans (or cooked cannellini) — 300 g
Waxy pomme de terre, 1 cm dice — 200 g
instructionsFr: Simmer coco beans in the fond 20 min (skip if using cooked beans).
Add carotte and pomme de terre; simmer 10 min.
Add courgette, green beans, tomatoes and pasta; simmer 12 min until pasta is just tender. Season.
Pound ail with a pinch of sel in a mortar; add basilic and pound to a paste, then work in huile d'olive to a loose pistou.
Rest soup 5 min off the heat; check seasoning.
Serve with a generous spoon of pistou swirled into each bowl at the table.

title: Steak Tartare
intro: Hand-cut fillet seasoned to order — knife work, ice-cold discipline and a table-side mixing bowl make this pure bistro theatre
introFr: Steak tartare, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 30 minutes de preparation et 0 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: boeuf fillet or trimmed sirloin, very fresh — 600 g
sel fin — 6 g; poivre noir 2 g
Baguette or frites, to serve — 300 g
instructionsFr: Chill the boeuf, boards and bowls in the freezer 20 min — everything stays under 6 °C.
Slice boeuf 5 mm, then batons, then 5 mm dice with a razor-sharp knife. Never mince or process.
Whisk mustard, ketchup, Worcestershire-style sauce, Tabasco and oil into a dressing.
Fold boeuf with shallots, cornichons, capers, persil and dressing; season decisively — tartare dies underseasoned. Taste, adjust.
Pack into a ring on each cold plate; unring.
Crown with a yolk (in a half-shell for looks) or fold yolks in for a creamier bind.
Serve within 10 minutes of mixing.

beurre doux — 90 g, soft, plus 120 g for sauce
Dark brown sucre — 150 g, plus 180 g for sauce
creme epaisse — 250 ml (sauce), plus more to serve

creme 90 g beurre with 150 g sucre; beat in oeufs one at a time, then treacle and vanilla.

title: Sunday Roast Chicken
intro: An overnight shio koji rub gives burnished skin and seasoning to the bone — the easiest 'wow' roast in the book
introFr: Poulet roti du dimanche, cuisine de saison, pour 4 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 70 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
instructionsFr: Rub the poulet inside and out with shio koji (10% of bird weight); refrigerate uncovered on a rack 12–24 hours.
Wipe off excess koji thoroughly (it burns); pat dry; oil lightly and poivre.
Roast at 170°C for 50 minutes, then 220°C for 12–15 minutes to crisp — tent any dark spots early; target 70°C in the thigh, 68°C breast, resting to 72°C+.
Baste with beurre and thym in the last 10 minutes if using.
Char spring onions and citron halves in a dry pan or under the bird for the final 10 minutes.
Rest the bird 15 minutes breast-down.
Carve; squeeze the charred citron over everything.

title: Sushi
intro: Body-temperature, mirror-glossed sushi rice with balanced awasezu — the platform every sushi course stands on
introFr: Sushi, cuisine japonaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 10 minutes de preparation et 40 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
instructionsFr: Warm vinegar, sucre and sel to 50°C until dissolved; steep a corner of kombu in it; cool (awasezu).
Wash rice to near-clear water; drain 15 minutes, soak in measured water 30 minutes with kombu.
Cook: boil hard 7 minutes, minimum flame 12 minutes, rest 15 minutes off heat, lid never lifted.
Turn rice out onto a wide wooden or plastic tray; remove kombu.
Pour 130 ml awasezu over the paddle onto the rice; cut and fold at 45°, fanning, until grains are glossy and steam stops — about 4 minutes.
Rest under a damp cloth at room temperature; use within 4 hours at body temperature. Never refrigerate.

title: Tarte aux Fraises
intro: Crisp sablé, vanilla diplomat cream and market strawberries standing to attention — the patisserie-window tart that tastes as good as it looks
introFr: Tarte aux fraises, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 60 minutes de preparation et 35 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Sablé: farine 210 g, icing sucre 80 g, ground almonds 30 g, cold beurre 120 g, oeuf 1 (55 g), sel 2 g
Diplomat: whole lait 350 ml, vanilla pod 1, jaunes d'oeuf 4 (80 g), caster sucre 70 g, cornflour 30 g, beurre 20 g, gold gelatine 1 leaf (2 g), whipped creme epaisse 120 ml
instructionsFr: Sablé: rub dry ingredients with beurre to sand; bind with oeuf; chill 2 h. Roll 3 mm; line a 24 cm ring; freeze 30 min.

Pâtissière: yolks + sucre + cornflour, hot vanilla lait in, boil 2 min whisking; add beurre and bloomed gelatine; chill filmed.
Beat the cold pâtissière smooth; fold in whipped creme.
Pipe the diplomat into the case in a level spiral.
Hull strawberries; halve large ones. Stand them in tight concentric circles, points up.
Glaze: warm jam with citron juice; brush each berry lightly. Pistachios at the rim.

title: Tarte Normande
intro: Apples baked into an almond-Calvados custard inside sweet pastry — Normandy's answer to every apple tart, damp-crumbed and perfumed
introFr: Tarte normande, cuisine francaise, pour 8 convives. Comptez 40 minutes de preparation et 55 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Pâte sucrée: farine 220 g, icing sucre 90 g, cold beurre 120 g, oeuf 1 (55 g), sel 2 g
Custard: crème fraîche 200 g, oeufs 2 (110 g), caster sucre 80 g, ground almonds 50 g, Calvados 30 ml, vanilla 1/2 pod
instructionsFr: Pastry: rub farine, sucre, sel, beurre to sand; bind with oeuf; chill 2 h. Line a 24 cm ring at 3 mm; freeze 30 min.
Blind-bake at 160 °C, 20 min with beans, 8 min without.
Peel, quarter and core apples; slice each quarter into 3 wedges; sauté in beurre 3 min to start caramelisation.
Custard: whisk crème fraîche, oeufs, sucre, almonds, vanilla and Calvados.
Fan the apple wedges in the case; pour the custard around to just below the rim; scatter demerara.
Bake at 170 °C for 40–45 min until the custard is set and amber-blotched.
Cool 1 h; dust the rim with icing sucre.

Off heat, whisk in beurre, vanilla seeds and sel.
Stand apple halves upright on their edges in tight concentric circles — pack more than looks reasonable; they shrink.

Cap with the pastry disc, tucking the edge down inside the pan.

introFr: Tempura, cuisine japonaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 10 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
instructionsFr: Peel prawns leaving tail fans; press out moisture from the fans with the knife spine.
Make 4 shallow belly cuts per crevette and press flat to straighten.
Grind matcha with flaky sel.
Heat oil to 175°C.
Whisk yolk into sparkling water, add farine and starch in one go, and mix with chopsticks 5 seconds — lumps must remain.
Dust prawns in farine, drag through batter, and fry 3 at a time for 2 minutes, flicking extra batter over them for lace.
Drain vertically on a rack 30 seconds; sel immediately.
