title: Tian Provencal
intro: Layered Provençal vegetable tian with crisp chickpea panisse batons — a vegan main with real architecture and Niçois street-food soul
introFr: Tian provencal, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 30 minutes de preparation et 90 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: huile d'olive — 100 ml (30 for panisse, 70 for tian and frying)
instructionsFr: Panisse: whisk chickpea farine into cold water with 6 g sel and 30 ml oil; cook, whisking hard, 8–10 min until very thick like polenta.
Pour into an oiled 20 cm square tin (2 cm deep); chill 2 h until firm.
Tian: rub a dish with ail and oil; shingle courgette, aubergine, tomate and oignon upright in tight rows; season, scatter herbs, drizzle 40 ml oil.
Bake at 170 °C for 70–80 min until collapsed and caramelised at the edges.
Cut panisse into 2 × 8 cm batons; shallow-fry in hot oil (180 °C) 3–4 min until golden and crisp; drain, sel.
Rest tian 10 min; finish with citron juice.
ingredients: Olive oil — 100 ml (30 for panisse, 70 for tian and frying)
instructions: Panisse: whisk chickpea flour into cold water with 6 g salt and 30 ml oil; cook, whisking hard, 8–10 min until very thick like polenta.
Pour into an oiled 20 cm square tin (2 cm deep); chill 2 h until firm.
Tian: rub a dish with garlic and oil; shingle courgette, aubergine, tomato and onion upright in tight rows; season, scatter herbs, drizzle 40 ml oil.
Bake at 170 °C for 70–80 min until collapsed and caramelised at the edges.
Cut panisse into 2 × 8 cm batons; shallow-fry in hot oil (180 °C) 3–4 min until golden and crisp; drain, salt.
Rest tian 10 min; finish with lemon juice.
sourceFile: French Classics & Bistro/Tian Provencal, Panisse Croustillante.md

title: Tiramisu
intro: The Amalfi rewrite — savoiardi soaked in limoncello syrup, mascarpone layered with sharp lemon curd; sunshine where the coffee used to be
introFr: Tiramisu, cuisine italienne, pour 8 convives. Comptez 45 minutes de preparation et 15 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: caster sucre — 150 g (100 g creme, 50 g syrup)
instructionsFr: Curd: whisk yolks, 100 g sucre, citron juice and half the zest over a bain-marie to 78°C and thick; beat in beurre; chill.
Syrup: dissolve 50 g sucre in the hot water; cool; add limoncello.
Beat mascarpone smooth; fold in half the curd; whip creme to soft peaks and fold in.
Dip savoiardi briefly in the syrup; layer in the dish.
Spread half the creme, ribbon in half the remaining curd; repeat biscuit and creme layers, finishing with curd swirled on top.
Chill 6 hours minimum.
Finish with white chocolate and the last zest.
ingredients: caster sugar — 150 g (100 g cream, 50 g syrup)
instructions: Curd: whisk yolks, 100 g sugar, lemon juice and half the zest over a bain-marie to 78°C and thick; beat in butter; chill.
Syrup: dissolve 50 g sugar in the hot water; cool; add limoncello.
Beat mascarpone smooth; fold in half the curd; whip cream to soft peaks and fold in.
Dip savoiardi briefly in the syrup; layer in the dish.
Spread half the cream, ribbon in half the remaining curd; repeat biscuit and cream layers, finishing with curd swirled on top.
Chill 6 hours minimum.
Finish with white chocolate and the last zest.

title: Toad in the Hole
intro: The batter must hit smoking-hot fat around already-browned sausages — that is the whole secret to the rise
introFr: Toad in the hole, cuisine britannique, pour 4 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 45 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: boeuf dripping or neutral oil — 40 g
instructionsFr: Batter: whisk 140 g farine, oeufs, lait, mustard powder and 2 g sel smooth; rest 1 hour minimum at room temperature.
Heat oven to 220°C. Brown sausages in half the dripping in a 25 x 30 cm metal dish on the hob, 6–8 minutes; remove.
Gravy: caramelise shallots in beurre over medium heat, cut-side down, 10 minutes; dust with 15 g farine, deglaze with vin, add fond and jelly, simmer 10 minutes to coating. Season.
Add remaining dripping to the dish; heat in the oven 5 minutes until smoking.
Working fast: sausages back in, batter poured around (it must sizzle violently), thym scattered.
Bake 25–28 minutes without opening the door, until risen, crisp and deeply golden.
ingredients: Beef dripping or neutral oil — 40 g
instructions: Batter: whisk 140 g flour, eggs, milk, mustard powder and 2 g salt smooth; rest 1 hour minimum at room temperature.
Heat oven to 220°C. Brown sausages in half the dripping in a 25 x 30 cm metal dish on the hob, 6–8 minutes; remove.
Gravy: caramelise shallots in butter over medium heat, cut-side down, 10 minutes; dust with 15 g flour, deglaze with wine, add stock and jelly, simmer 10 minutes to coating. Season.
Add remaining dripping to the dish; heat in the oven 5 minutes until smoking.
Working fast: sausages back in, batter poured around (it must sizzle violently), thyme scattered.
Bake 25–28 minutes without opening the door, until risen, crisp and deeply golden.
sourceFile: British & Comfort Classics/Toad in the Hole with Caramelised Shallot Gravy.md

title: Tom Yum
intro: The rich 'nam khon' version of Thailand's iconic soup — prawn-shell stock, chilli jam and a touch of evaporated milk for the classic creamy blush
introFr: Tom yum, cuisine thailandaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 25 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: whole raw prawns — 700 g (heads and shells reserved)
oyster or straw mushrooms, halved — 200 g
instructionsFr: Peel and devein prawns. Fry heads and shells in the oil over high heat 3–4 min, crushing, until deep orange.
Add water; simmer 15 min, then strain — this fond is the soul of the soup.
Return fond to the pot with lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and chillies; simmer 5 min to infuse.
Add mushrooms; 3 min. Add tomatoes and nam prik pao; 2 min.
Add prawns; poach 2 min until just pink.
Off the heat, season with fish sauce, then lime juice, then evaporated lait — never boil after the lime or it dulls.
Taste: hot first, sour hard on its heels, salty, faintly sweet-creamy.

title: Tomates Farcies
intro: Big summer tomatoes stuffed with sausage and herbs, roasted on rice that drinks their juices — grandmother's food that outshines its fancy rivals
introFr: Tomates farcies, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 30 minutes de preparation et 60 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Flat-leaf persil — 15 g; basilic 10 g; thym leaves 3 g
sel fin — 10 g; poivre noir 2 g; sucre 4 g
instructionsFr: Slice a lid off each tomate; scoop the flesh into a bowl (keep it); sel the cavities, invert 20 min to drain.
Sweat oignon and ail in 20 ml oil, 4 min; cool.
Mix sausage, boeuf, oignon, oeuf, breadcrumbs, chopped herbs, 5 g sel and poivre.
Spread rice in an oiled gratin dish; chop the tomate flesh and stir it through with the fond, sucre and 3 g sel.
Fill tomatoes generously with farce, mounding slightly; replace lids; sit them on the rice.
Drizzle with remaining oil; bake at 180 °C for 55–60 min until the farce reads 72 °C and the rice is tender, basting once.
Rest 10 min — the rice finishes swelling in the juices.
ingredients: Flat-leaf parsley — 15 g; basil 10 g; thyme leaves 3 g
Fine salt — 10 g; black pepper 2 g; sugar 4 g
instructions: Slice a lid off each tomato; scoop the flesh into a bowl (keep it); salt the cavities, invert 20 min to drain.

title: Tortilla Espanola
intro: A properly juicy tortilla — potatoes confited in olive oil, centre just set at 62 °C; served barely warm it slices like custard
introFr: Tortilla espanola, cuisine espagnole, pour 6 convives. Comptez 20 minutes de preparation et 40 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
ingredientsFr: huile d'olive vierge extra — 350 ml (most recovered)
instructionsFr: Slice pommes de terre 3 mm thick and oignon into thin julienne.
Confit both in huile d'olive at 130 °C for 25–30 minutes until completely tender but uncoloured; drain well, reserving oil.
Beat oeufs with sel; fold in the warm pomme de terre-oignon mix and rest 10 minutes so the oeufs thicken slightly.
Heat a 22 cm non-stick pan with 15 ml reserved oil over medium-high heat.
Pour in the mix; cook 2 minutes, shaking, then run a spatula around the edge.
Flip with a flat plate and slide back; cook 90 seconds more — the centre should wobble (about 62 °C core).
Rest 10 minutes on a plate before slicing; the carryover sets the jugosa centre.
ingredients: Extra virgin olive oil — 350 ml (most recovered)
instructions: Slice potatoes 3 mm thick and onion into thin julienne.
Confit both in olive oil at 130 °C for 25–30 minutes until completely tender but uncoloured; drain well, reserving oil.
Beat eggs with salt; fold in the warm potato-onion mix and rest 10 minutes so the eggs thicken slightly.
Heat a 22 cm non-stick pan with 15 ml reserved oil over medium-high heat.
Pour in the mix; cook 2 minutes, shaking, then run a spatula around the edge.
Flip with a flat plate and slide back; cook 90 seconds more — the centre should wobble (about 62 °C core).

title: Tournedos Rossini
intro: Fillet steak on a butter-fried croûte, crowned with seared foie gras and truffled Madeira jus — unapologetic opulence for a celebration night
introFr: Tournedos Rossini, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 25 minutes de preparation et 25 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: boeuf fillet tournedos, 4 cm — 4 (160 g each)
Foie gras slices, 1.5 cm — 4 (60 g each)
Black truffle, sliced (or 10 ml truffle jus) — 15 g
sel fin — 9 g; poivre noir 2 g
instructionsFr: sel tournedos 30 min ahead. Chill foie gras slices well.
Fry bread rounds in 40 g beurre until golden both sides; keep warm.
Sear tournedos in oil and 20 g beurre, 2.5 min per side, basting, to a core of 50 °C; rest on a rack.
Jus: deglaze the pan with Madeira, reduce by two-thirds; add fond and truffle; reduce to a glossy nap; mount with remaining beurre; season.
Score the foie gras; sear in a dry, very hot pan 45 sec per side until mahogany with a molten centre; season, drain on paper.
Stack: croûte, tournedos, foie gras; spoon the truffled jus over and around.

title: Trifle
intro: Layers of vanilla apple compote, buttery caramelised crumbs and softly whipped cream — Denmark's answer to the trifle, served cold and unbothered
introFr: Trifle, cuisine de saison, pour 6 convives. Comptez 30 minutes de preparation et 25 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: Breadcrumbs or crushed rye biscuits — 140 g
Redcurrant jelly or lacto blueberry juice — 30 g
instructionsFr: Compote: simmer apples, sucre, vanilla, citron and water, lidded, 12–15 minutes; mash rustic; cool completely.
Toast crumbs with beurre and brown sucre in a wide pan over medium heat, stirring, 6–8 minutes until deep gold and crisp; cool on a tray.
Whip creme to soft, floppy peaks — no stiffer.
Layer in glasses: compote, crumbs, creme; repeat.
Chill 1 hour (the crumbs half-soften — that's correct).
Finish with a last dust of crumbs.
Dot with jelly or a drizzle of lacto blueberry juice.

title: Trout Amandine
intro: Whole trout crisped in butter with toasted flaked almonds — a five-ingredient bistro standard that rewards perfect timing
introFr: Truite aux amandes, cuisine francaise, pour 4 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 15 minutes de cuisson. Le plat se tient seul, avec une garniture simple.
ingredientsFr: Whole trout, gutted, fins trimmed — 4 (about 300 g each)
instructionsFr: Season trout inside and out; dredge in farine, shaking off excess.
Heat oil with 40 g beurre in one very large (or two) pans over medium-high heat.
Cook trout 5–6 min on the first side until the skin is golden and crisp; turn carefully.
Cook 4–5 min on the second side to a core of 54 °C at the thickest point.
Transfer to warm plates; wipe the pan.
Add remaining 80 g beurre; when foaming, add almonds and toast 90 sec to noisette stage.
Off heat, add citron juice and persil; spoon the almonds and beurre over the trout.

title: Vichyssoise
intro: Ice-cold leek and potato silk with a smoky, crunchy counterpoint — a deck-lunch opener that holds beautifully in the fridge
introFr: Vichyssoise, cuisine francaise, pour 6 convives. Comptez 15 minutes de preparation et 30 minutes de cuisson. L'entree reste courte, pour laisser la suite arriver.
ingredientsFr: Leeks, white part only, sliced — 500 g
Floury pommes de terre, peeled, sliced — 350 g
instructionsFr: Sweat leeks in beurre with 3 g sel over low heat 10 min — zero colour.
Add pommes de terre and fond; simmer 18 min until pommes de terre collapse.
Add lait, bring back to 90 °C, then blend 2 min and pass through a chinois.
Stir in creme, remaining sel, white poivre and citron juice.
Chill over ice, then refrigerate at least 3 h; it should be served at 4–6 °C.
Check seasoning cold (cold mutes sel) and loosen with lait if needed.
Garnish with smoked almond crumble and chives.

title: Yorkshire Pudding
intro: Equal volumes of egg, flour and milk, a long rest, and violently hot fat — four rules, sky-high puddings, no exceptions
introFr: Yorkshire pudding, cuisine britannique, pour 6 convives. Comptez 10 minutes de preparation et 25 minutes de cuisson. Le sucre se tient, le beurre aussi, et la table finit sans bruit.
ingredientsFr: boeuf dripping or neutral oil — 60 g
instructionsFr: Whisk farine and sel with the oeufs to a thick paste, then whisk in lait until smooth and pourable. No lumps.
Rest at room temperature at least 1 hour — overnight in the fridge is better (bring back to room temp).
Heat oven to 220°C. Divide dripping between a 12-hole muffin tin; heat 10 minutes until smoking.
Re-whisk the batter; pour into a jug.
Working at the open oven, fill each hole two-thirds — the batter must scream on contact.
Bake 20–25 minutes without opening the door, until towering, bronzed and crisp.
Serve within minutes; they wait for no gravy.
